findings.title: E1 survives: no test pins where the FC1(a) isascii guard sits (any non-ASCII PEM-prefixed key gets past every row)
findings.evidence: Every R3 non-ASCII param (bom-pem, smart-quoted-pem, zwsp-pem) has its non-ASCII character at the START. None of them can reach the `text.startswith(_PEM_PREFIX)` branch, so nothing pins the guard's position before that branch. Measured with the mutant on the exact bytes. E1 moves the guard after the PEM branch, into the base64 branch. With -k r3_: `[pyt] tag=rv2-mut-E1 start=2026-10-18 04:17:43 end=2026-10-18 04:17:47 elapsed=3s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 11 passed, 100 deselected. Against both unit files with all nodes: `[pyt] tag=rv2-mut-E1F start=2026-10-18 04:18:17 end=2026-10-18 04:18:22 elapsed=6s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 119 passed. My variant E9 checks only the first character (`text[:1].isascii()`): `[pyt] tag=rv2-mut-E9 start=2026-10-18 04:18:22 end=2026-10-18 04:18:27 elapsed=5s status=OK rc=0`, 119 passed. Effect, from probe_fc1.out (plain python -I, module loaded by path, no pytest, no network). Committed bytes: pem-trailing-smart-quote, pem-nbsp-inside and pem-zwsp-inside-body each give `type=ValueError const_msg=True context=NoneType cause=NoneType key_fragments_in_chain=0`. E1 and E9: the trailing-smart-quote and NBSP forms give `NO EXCEPTION (secret built)`, so a corrupted key is silently accepted. The ZWSP-in-body form gives `type=ValueError const_msg=False context=ValueError`, so the cryptography error comes back with __context__ attached (0 key fragments measured). There is no leak on the committed bytes; the gap is that the FC1(a) 'refuse non-ASCII before any decoding' guarantee has no row protecting it on the PEM path. This confirms the cut-off run's E1 survival.
findings.fix: Add PEM-prefixed non-ASCII params to R3's `_bad_key_forms`. Add the same params to `_NON_ASCII_FORMS`: `pem-trailing-smart-quote` (pem.strip() + '”'), `pem-nbsp-inside` (a U+00A0 before a newline) and `pem-zwsp-inside-body` (a U+200B inside the first body line). Each must give ValueError from both build_client_secret and _normalise_private_key, plus `_assert_clean_value_error`, no key text in the chain, and spy.calls == 0. The probe shows this row is green on the committed bytes and kills E1 and E9.

findings.title: E10 survives: no test reaches the UnicodeDecodeError arm of GB5/FC1 (base64 that decodes to non-ASCII bytes)
findings.evidence: No R3 or R9 key form base64-decodes to non-ASCII bytes. garbage fails with binascii.Error; the base64 and labelled forms decode to ASCII. So the UnicodeDecodeError branch that GB5 rules on is never exercised. E10 narrows the except to `except binascii.Error:`. Both unit files, all nodes: `[pyt] tag=rv2-mut-E10 start=2026-10-18 04:18:28 end=2026-10-18 04:18:33 elapsed=5s bound=600s status=OK rc=0`, 119 passed. Effect, from probe_fc1.out, for form base64-of-der-p8 (base64 of the PKCS#8 DER of a generated P-256 key, a plausible mistake by the owner). Committed bytes: `type=ValueError const_msg=True context=NoneType cause=NoneType key_fragments_in_chain=0`, log `WARNING [SIWA] client secret build failed: ValueError`. E10: `type=UnicodeDecodeError const_msg=False ... key_fragments_in_chain=2`, because the DER private-key bytes sit in the exception's .object and args. The log line becomes `client secret build failed: UnicodeDecodeError`, which breaks the spec 2.9 template. The committed bytes are correct. Nothing protects this arm, and it is the same leak class FC1 closed (RV-SEC-4).
findings.fix: Add an R3 `_bad_key_forms` param `base64-of-der-p8`: base64 of key.private_bytes(DER, PKCS8, NoEncryption) for the generated key. It must give ValueError from both functions, `_assert_clean_value_error`, no key text or DER bytes in the chain (extend `_assert_no_key_text_in_exception` to check bytes args and .object), and spy.calls == 2. Optionally add an R9 param that asserts the log line `[SIWA] client secret build failed: ValueError`. This kills E10.

findings.title: E11 survives (validate=True dropped from b64decode): the key reader becomes more lenient, nothing leaks
findings.evidence: `[pyt] tag=rv2-mut-E11 start=2026-10-18 04:18:33 end=2026-10-18 04:18:38 elapsed=5s status=OK rc=0`, 119 passed. On the committed bytes, a quoted base64 value (`"<b64 of pem>"`) is refused with a constant ValueError (probe_fc1.out, committed base64-quoted). A lenient decode would accept it. The PEM-prefix check and the constant-error mapping still apply, so no leak path exists.
findings.fix: Optional: add an R3 param `base64-quoted` that expects ValueError.
